application_guidance.input_pattern: A worst-case dimension-free deterministic first-order stationarity question with bounded initial function gap and both gradient and Hessian regularity.
read_original_when: Changing Oracle, algorithm class, output convention, norm, parameter window or dimension regime.
Reusing the hard instance or its gradient/smoothness estimates: read Appendices B.1–B.2 and Part I's resisting-oracle argument.
sensitive_conditions: Both derivative budgets must be fixed; Hessian regularity alone is a different function class.
Finite dimension is allowed to grow with the hardness length.
The source measures hitting among iterates; additional output conventions need a separate checked transfer.
The deterministic lifting does not establish unrestricted randomized Oracle Complexity.

complexity_scope.guarantee: Worst-case inf-method/sup-instance hitting-complexity lower bound over finite but unbounded dimension.
complexity_scope.hidden_constants: Universal positive constants c and ell1,ell2. They are not explicit numerical constants in this extracted statement.
complexity_scope.oracle: Exact function-value and gradient response at each query; no higher-derivative response.
complexity_scope.output_and_metric: First iterate/query index with Euclidean gradient norm <=epsilon, as defined by Section 2.3. No separate claim about unqueried terminal outputs is added.
complexity_scope.resource: First-order query/iterate index in the source model; each query returns value and gradient. Arithmetic work and direct Hessian access are not charged or covered by this statement.
complexity_scope.upper_witness_or_lower_coverage: All deterministic first-order methods, plus the source's first-order zero-respecting class. Support restriction belongs to the zero-respecting construction analysis; Proposition 1 provides deterministic lifting.

content.intended_use: A source lower bound separating deterministic first-order stationarity complexity from higher-order access under Hessian regularity.

proofs.locator: Section 4, PDF pp.11–12; Section 5.2 equations (11)–(16), pp.15–16; Functions with Lipschitz Hessian, p.18; Proposition 1, p.6; Theorem 1 equation (8a), p.9
map: Source construction, equations (9)–(10), p.11: bar f_{T,mu,r}(x)=sqrt(mu)(x1-1)^2/2 + (1/2)sum_{i=1}^T(x_{i+1}-x_i)^2 + mu sum_{i=1}^T Upsilon_r(x_i), where Upsilon_r(x)=120 integral_1^x t^2(t-1)/(1+(t/r)^2) dt. T is a positive integer, 0<mu<=1, r>=1, and x lies in R^(T+1).

Observation 2 and Lemma 3, p.12: the instance is a first-order zero-chain and ||grad bar f||>mu^(3/4)/4 whenever x_T=x_{T+1}=0. The source sketches a transition-length dichotomy; the detailed Appendix B.2 Proof was not read. Observation 1, p.6, forces these terminal zeros for zero-respecting iterates t<=T.

Lemma 4, p.12: initial gap <=sqrt(mu)/2+10mu T; qth derivative Lipschitz constant <=(1_{q=1}+r^(3-q)mu)ell_q. Rescale f(x)=lambda sigma^2 bar f(x/sigma), equation (11), p.15. Equations (12)–(15), pp.15–16, impose smoothness, choose T=floor((Delta-lambda sqrt(mu)sigma^2/2)/(10lambda mu sigma^2)), and require lambda mu^(3/4)sigma>=4epsilon to obtain the hitting lower bound.

For p=2, p.18 keeps equation (16): bar ell1=2ell1; bar ell2=max{ell2,4(2ell1)^2}; bar Lq=Lq/bar ellq. Set lambda=bar L1, r=1, mu=bar L2 sigma/lambda, sigma=(4 bar L1^(-1/4) bar L2^(-3/4) epsilon)^(4/7). The accuracy condition ensures mu<=1. In the branch lambda sqrt(mu)sigma^2<=Delta, equation (15) gives Delta bar L1^(3/7)bar L2^(2/7)/(20*4^(12/7)*epsilon^(12/7)).

For the complementary gap branch, p.18 compares the target rate to the convex quadratic lower bound sqrt(Delta L1)/(4epsilon) from Theorem 1, equation (8a), p.9. Thus no extra lower bound on Delta is needed. Proposition 1, p.6, transfers zero-respecting hardness to arbitrary deterministic first-order methods through orthogonal invariance and dimension freedom.

assumptions: The class is F_{1:2}(Delta,L1,L2) as defined above, with both smoothness budgets imposed globally.
Only function values and gradients are supplied by the Oracle.
The covered algorithm class is A_det^(1) union A_zr^(1), exactly as in the source.
0<epsilon<=L1^2/L2; no additional small-Delta exclusion is imposed by the statement.
statement.conclusion: T_epsilon(A_det^(1) union A_zr^(1), F_{1:2}(Delta,L1,L2)) >= c Delta (L1/ell1)^(3/7)(L2/ell2)^(2/7) epsilon^(-12/7). Thus the dependence is Omega(Delta L1^(3/7)L2^(2/7)epsilon^(-12/7)) with a universal implicit constant.
statement.objects_and_definitions: F_{1:2}(Delta,L1,L2)=F_1(Delta,L1) intersection F_2(Delta,L2), a union over all finite dimensions of C-infinity functions f:R^d->R satisfying f(0)-inf f<=Delta. For q=1,2 the source's smoothness convention is: for every x, unit v, and real t,t', the line restriction g(t)=f(x+tv) satisfies |g^(q)(t)-g^(q)(t')|<=Lq|t-t'|. All vector norms are Euclidean. A_det^(1) consists of measurable deterministic first-order methods using preceding values and gradients; A_zr^(1) consists of first-order methods satisfying supp(x^(t)) subset union_{s<t} supp(grad f(x^(s))). Define T_epsilon(A,f)=inf{t in N: ||grad f(x^(t))||<=epsilon}, and class complexity as inf over methods of sup over functions.
statement.parameter_domains: Delta,L1,L2>0; epsilon in (0,L1^2/L2]. Constants c,C,ell_q are independent of these parameters and dimension.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: There exist universal positive numerical constants c,C and positive ell_q for q in N, with ell_q<=exp((3q/2)log q+Cq), such that for every Delta,L1,L2>0 and every 0<epsilon<=L1^2/L2 the displayed minimax lower bound holds. Dimension is not fixed; the worst-case supremum ranges over finite dimensions. No unrestricted randomized-method probability guarantee is asserted.
